_provenance.selected_on: VizWiz-VQA train split, first 400 reading questions (ocr-plan.md section 2 forbids tuning on the 577 validation images)
_provenance.selected_by: train.ocr.measure Stage 3 screen, five configurations, same scoring rule as the captioner
why: canvas_size 2560 (EasyOCR's default) cost 3.36 s/run against 0.70 s/run at 1600 with no measurable accuracy difference: 45 vs 46 hits out of 400, against a standard error of about 1.6 percentage points. The 4.8x speedup is the only statistically solid finding.
1600px covers the median validation image (long side 1296 px) without the detector downscaling it, which is why the reduction is cheap.
mag_ratio 1.0 rather than 1.5: the extra magnification pass is the second-most expensive knob and did not separate the configurations.

The lenient detector thresholds (text 0.6, link 0.35, low_text 0.35 against EasyOCR's 0.7/0.4/0.4) had the joint-highest hit count and the fewest images with no text at all (71 of 400). Dense small text is the recall problem here -- sign/screen and label/packaging are 56 percent of the reading bucket -- so admitting weaker boxes is the direction worth leaning.
This file deliberately pins no 'preprocess' key, so --pipelines none,enhance stay distinct and the measurement reports both with identical engine parameters.
